about: The pile-order rules the state key obeys (docs/rebuild/FIGHT_SOLVER.md section 2). tools/solver/scan_order_reads.py finds every read of a pile's index or position in CardEffects, RelicEffects, PotionEffects, BuffSystem, CombatEngine and EnemyAI (order_reads.json); this file classes each read of a pile the key writes as a multiset (hand, discard, exhaust, potion slots): by kind through 'rules', else in 'sites' as reader (its category's cards, relics or potions keep the pile ordered), roll (hindsight mode keeps the pile ordered), flow (carries the hand's order into another pile: see 'implies'), free (with why) or dead (no caller). KeyFieldCoverageTests fails on an unclassed read, a stale class, a scan older than the sources, a reader whose holders are not its category's, or a dead method with a caller. A category is on while the combat holds one of its cards (any pile, queue or screen) or an active relic, or always; 'implies' turns on the categories whose order flows into it.

potions.name: KingsCourage
potions.why: found by KeyBisimulationTests, not by a per-site read: on core2 (F08, F10) using it from a position whose exhaust pile is permuted steps to another key. The scan now reaches Forge from this potion (holder potion:KingsCourage) and the walks there are classed free, so the difference is in core2 code that Forge reaches, which the scan classes out by file (Core2/OldState.cs builds the kernel card table by walking the piles in order): the potion stays a reader until that read is classed per site

potion_slot.why: the scan found no rule that reads a potion's slot beyond the action's own slot argument and the first empty slot

enemy_order.why: acting order is slot order, and an untargeted effect takes the first targetable enemy (CombatEngine's default target, CardEffects' FirstOrDefault(IsTargetable) sites): every combat has a reader until the S3 harness shows which positions do not, so EnemyClasses keeps every enemy distinct

hindsight_ordered.why: hindsight mode keys the streams, so a roll's index lands on a fixed position: every pile a roll indexes (class or kind roll) stays ordered, and every pile whose order flows into one (implies); that is all four multiset piles

screen.why: a screen's candidates are pile indices, and the key keeps every pile ordered while a screen is open

roll.why: an index from a roll over the pile or a list filtered from it: in expected mode every position is equally likely, so permuting the pile moves no probability (hindsight mode keeps the pile ordered)
